column1: # manifests/magnetar-substrate-keep.tsv
# Extra d-i udebs the MAGNETAR (server) medium must keep even though they are
# not part of the d-i initrd's already-unpacked set and are not one of the NIC
# driver udebs preseed/early_command installs by path.
# Format: <package>\t<reason>            (blank lines and '#' comments ignored)
# This list only ADDS keeps. slim_installer_pool() in
# build/iso/write-usb-image.py (opt-in: NCZ_MAGNETAR_SLIM_SUBSTRATE=1) drops
# nothing but the provable classes in magnetar_substrate.provable_drop_reason();
# every other pooled udeb stays whether it is listed here or not. A row here
# also protects a provable-class udeb from being dropped.
# The measured numbers below describe the earlier minimal keep-set, which was
# disproved (see docs/MAGNETAR-SERVER-VARIANT.md, "Review correction").
# Measured reference set (amd64, substrate 2026-10-13, d-i initrd
# 7.2.9+deb14): 45 of the 231 pooled udebs are already unpacked in the initrd
# (anna never fetches them from the medium), and 5 NIC module udebs are
# installed by early_command. The five openssh/udpkg udebs come from
# assets/ssh-udebs/ (baked into the initrd) and are ALSO pooled, so the
# diag-console.sh by-path lookup keeps working whether it scans /ncz/ssh-udebs
# or /cdrom.
# Why the openssh stack is not dropped outright: preseed/diag-console.sh
# install_sshd_udebs() udpkg-installs libc6-udeb zlib1g-udeb libcrypt1-udeb
# libcrypto3-udeb openssh-client-udeb openssh-server-udeb from the first
# media it can find. The first three/four are already initrd builtins, but
# openssh-*-udeb are not, and their by-path lookup scans /cdrom too. Dropping
# them would silently degrade installer-side remote diagnostics -- the exact
# thing diag-console.sh exists to prevent -- for ~1 MB. Keep them.
openssh-client-udeb
column2: diag-console.sh install_sshd_udebs() udpkg-installs it by path; remote installer diagnostics must not depend on the network

column1: openssh-server-udeb
column2: diag-console.sh install_sshd_udebs() udpkg-installs it by path; remote installer diagnostics must not depend on the network

column1: # MEASURED COMPRESSIBILITY (2026-10-17, amd64 substrate 2026-10-13, `tar -cf |
# xz -6 -T0` over the pool). udebs are .deb archives whose payload is already
# xz, so a second pass recovers ~0.1%:
# Therefore compressing the substrate pool buys nothing worth a retriever fork:
# cdrom-retriever/anna fetch a udeb PATH from an apt index and dpkg-deb reads
# the file itself, so a .tar.xz pool would need a custom retriever and would
# break load-cdrom -- the one path this task must not break. The compression
# that pays is on the finished image (write-usb-image.py --compress), where FAT
# padding, ext4 free space and squashfs layering dominate.
